Potential Fields

Potential fields for robot motion planning. An attractive potential pulls the robot towards the goal at the origin: it grows quadratically up to the distance di (the red circle, where the two parts meet) and linearly beyond, with gain ζi. A repulsive potential pushes the robot away from an obstacle: it is 0 beyond the distance ρ0 and grows without bound at the obstacle, with gain ηi. The last two tabs add the attractive potential and two obstacles, as a surface and as a contour plot; drag the two pads to move the obstacles. (This caption is the port's: the lecture notebook has none.)

Details

The potentials, as defined in the notebook, with the robot at (x, y), its distance D from the goal at the origin and its distance ρ from an obstacle: Uatt = ½ ζ D² for D ≤ d and d ζ (D − ½ d) beyond; Urep = ½ η (1/ρ − 1/ρ0)² for ρ ≤ ρ0 and 0 beyond. A robot following the negative gradient of the sum slides towards the goal and around the obstacles, unless it stops in a local minimum. In the last two tabs η = 1 and ρ0 = 2.

Port notes: the heights above the plot range are cut off as Mathematica does (a flat, light top on the surfaces; white in the contour plot); the red curves in the last two tabs mark where the notebook's If conditions switch, as Mathematica's ExclusionsStyle -> Red draws them. See the design document for how the automatic height range is chosen.

Browser port of a Mathematica notebook. All computation runs in your browser.
